messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The “largest” planet depends on what you’re looking at:

| Category | Largest Known Object | Size (≈) |
|----------|----------------------|----------|
| **Planet in our Solar System** | Jupiter | 11.2 R⊕ (≈ 1.1 R_J) |
| **Largest confirmed exoplanet** | HD 100546 b (a protoplanet) | ≈ 2.5 R_J (about 25 % larger than Jupiter) |
| **Largest “hot Jupiter”** | WASP‑17b | ≈ 1.5 R_J (inflated due to proximity to its star) |

So, within our own Solar System, Jupiter is the biggest. Across the entire observable universe, the most massive and largest‑radius planet discovered so far is the protoplanet HD 100546 b, which is still forming around its young star. If you’re interested in the largest fully‑formed gas giant, WASP‑17b is the record holder.
